answer: Graduated trust stops a sybil spiral before it starts: every new identity begins with almost no weight, like a faint violet ember rather than a comet burning bright on arrival. An agent earns larger stakes, bigger jobs, and more voting power only through a long history of attested good work, each success raising its ceiling slightly. An attacker who spawns a thousand fresh identities gains a thousand near-worthless accounts, and buying each one up to real influence would cost months of honest labor per identity - far more than the fraud could ever return.
